Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/768
- **Title**: gh-766 [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-766` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +310
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #766
### Root Cause

A dead PR at mergeBot's FIFO head never yielded its position: a `blocked`-labeled PR was skipped with a bare silent `continue`, and an armed PR with checks pending forever just logged `checks=pending — waiting` on every tick. Every approved PR behind it stayed `FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)` — `acted: 0` for over an hour while 4 approved+validated PRs sat behind `pr-1231` (live, run 37456658085+).

### Fix

- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`:
  - `blocked` head → explicit skip line `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked` (fa #939 semantics preserved — still never acted on); closed PRs were already invisible (open-only listing).
  - Armed **approved** head whose checks have been motionless past `jobParams.staleHeadMinutes` (default 120 = 2h; measured from the oldest pending check run's `started_at`, workflow-run fallback included, missing timestamps fail open) → skip line + unarm `ai_validating`, freeing the SM's validate-armed mutex. Dev-lane arms keep waiting untouched (mutexAmong parity).
  - The first approved PR behind skipped heads that carries the `ai_validated` latch takes the vacated position and merges on the **same evidence gates as the armed path** (green rollup on current head + `CLEAN`). One advance per skip-chain — FIFO holds for everyone behind; never-validated / mid-review / conflicted PRs keep deferring.
  - Metric: `skipped` counter in the result + `heads skipped: N` in the final log line.
- `rollupDetail()` extracted from `checksRollup()` (returns `{ state, pendingSince }`); `checksRollup` behavior unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- `test_mergeBot.js` new suite `dead FIFO head must not starve the queue (gh-766)`: acceptance `[blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → pr-2 merges + head skip line`, stale-pending unarm+advance, fresh-pending no-race, no-timestamp fail-open, live-head regression, BEHIND candidate no-jump, `staleHeadMinutes` knob — RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Full suite: **1663 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No SM changes: the bot still only concludes stages whose evidence is already on the PR (merge = approved + validated-latch + green-on-current-head + CLEAN); `mergeStateOf`/`squashMerge` gates are reused verbatim.
- A permanently stuck head now re-validates at most once per threshold period (unarm → SM re-arm) while the queue drains past it each time — bounded CI cost.

# gh-766: [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)

## Description

## Проблема (never-again)

factory-merge.yml (mergeBot) ставит approved PR в FIFO-очередь «awaiting validate-armed turn»; если PR в **голове** очереди никогда не получает validate-armed turn (заблокирован лейблом `blocked` владельцем / checks=pending навсегда / ревьюерский лимб), **вся очередь мёртва за ним**: `acted: 0`, ни один готовый PR не мержится.

Дважды подтверждено в бою на flutter_agent_harness 2026-10-06:
- Утром: pr-1304 approved висел «FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)», очередь стояла, смержился только после ручного вмешательства владельца.
- Днём (run 37456658085 и позже): голова `pr-1231 checks=pending — waiting` (заблокированный владельцем дубль), за ним 4 approved+validated PR (1309, 1311, 1313, 1317) — `acted: 0` на каждом тике больше часа.

## Корень

mergeBot не выкидывает из очереди PR, которые заведомо не получат слот: лейбл `blocked`, checks=pending без движения N часов, closed/superseded. FIFO-голова становится poison pill.

## Предлагаемый фикс

1. На каждом тике голова очереди проверяется на «живость»: `blocked` label / closed / checks=pending старше порога (напр. 2ч) → **skip с явным логом** (не drop молча — строка «⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked» в acted-лог).
2. Skipped PR не блокирует следующих: очередь продвигается к первому живому.
3. Метрика/лог: число пропущенных голов за тик — видно в логе рана (сейчас диагностика требует grep'ать «awaiting validate-armed turn» вручную).

## Acceptance

- Тест/симуляция: очередь [blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → тик мержит approved-2, в логе skip-строка про head.
- Регрессия: нормальный approved-head мержится как раньше.

## Machine jobs

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

## Understanding the change

### 1. `pendingStartedAt(r)` — new helper
Extracts epoch ms of when a run started (started_at/startedAt/created_at/createdAt). Returns null if unusable. Fails open.

### 2. `rollupDetail()` — extracted from `checksRollup()`
Returns `{ state, pendingSince }`. `checksRollup()` now wraps `rollupDetail().state`. Behavior unchanged.

Note there's a pre-existing weird line in `rollupDetail`:
```js
var runs = cr.check_runs || cr.total_count !== undefined ? (cr.check_runs || []) : [];
```
This is a pre-existing bug (operator precedence) — `cr.check_runs || (cr.total_count !== undefined) ? (cr.check_runs || []) : []`. If `cr.check_runs` is truthy → `(cr.check_runs || [])`. If falsy but `total_count !== undefined` → `[]` (since `cr.check_runs` falsy). If both falsy → `[]`. Actually the result is always `(cr.check_runs || [])` — because both branches of the ternary yield `(cr.check_runs || [])`. So it's a no-op ternary. Pre-existing though — NOT introduced by this PR. The PR didn't change that line. Out-of-diff but could be mentioned in general comments.

### 3. In `action()`:
- New `staleHeadMinutes` param (default 120).
- `skippedHeads` counter, `deadHeadPassed` flag.

Loop changes:
- **blocked label**: now logs `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked`, increments skippedHeads, sets `deadHeadPassed = true`, and continues. Previously bare `continue`.

- **non-validating (or mid-review) branch**: if approved and not agent:review:

But hold on — should the skip-chain state reset when encountering an armed PR? Consider: blocked head (deadHeadPassed=true), then a mid-review non-approved non-validating PR (the `!validating || agent:review` branch — if NOT approved, no advance attempt; deadHeadPassed stays true), then an armed PR (resets to false). Hmm, if the armed PR comes after, then reset. That seems intentional: the armed PR owns the FIFO position.

Sequence: armed live head → blocked → then validated candidate. deadHeadPassed gets set true at the blocked PR, which is AFTER the armed one. So the queue advances past the blocked PR to the validated one — correct per gh-766? Hmm, but wait — the ticket's premise: the head of the FIFO queue. The list is sorted by PR number (oldest first = FIFO). The "head" is the first PR. But `deadHeadPassed` doesn't track position; it tracks "some dead PR was skipped earlier in the list". So if there's a healthy armed PR #1 (older), a blocked PR #2, and a validated approved PR #3: tick processes #1 (armed, green, CLEAN, approved) → merges #1. Then #2 blocked → skip line, deadHeadPassed=true. Then #3 validated → advances and merges. So in one tick, TWO merges happen (#1 and #3). Is that intended? The ticket says "One advance per skip-chain". Actually merging both is arguably fine — #1 was ready to merge anyway. But does this violate the mutex semantics (one merge per tick)? Previously, could the bot merge more than one PR per tick? Looking at the loop: for each armed approved green CLEAN PR, it merges. Multiple armed PRs in one tick each merge (the mutex is maintained by SM, not the bot). Actually, the loop iterates all PRs; if several armed approved green CLEAN PRs exist (mutex violation), all merge. So multiple merges per tick are possible pre-existing. OK.

Processing: #1 → skip, deadHeadPassed=true. #2 → advance candidate, merges. deadHeadPassed consumed. #3 → armed, live, waits. Fine.

Processing: #1 skip → deadHeadPassed=true. #2: approved, no ai_validated → advance=false → FIFO-queued line; **deadHeadPassed remains true** (not consumed). #3: advance → merges. But the code only consumes `deadHeadPassed` when `advance` is true (i.e. when deadHeadPassed && ai_validated). If the first approved PR behind the dead head lacks `ai_validated`, it does NOT consume the slot, and the next validated PR takes it.   // VACATED the head position — the first approved PR behind them
  // that already carries validation evidence (the ai_validated
  // latch) takes the turn on the SAME evidence gates as the armed
  // path: green rollup on the current head + CLEAN. One advance
  // per skip-chain — the first candidate consumes it, so FIFO
  // holds for everyone behind; never-validated, mid-review,

"never-validated ... keep deferring" — meaning they defer but don't consume the slot. Hmm, but that means a validated PR can jump a never-validated approved PR that was queued earlier (FIFO violation in the strict sense). But arguably that's the point: the never-validated PR can't merge anyway (no validation evidence), so letting a fully-evidenced PR merge is the desired outcome. The ticket says "Skipped PR не блокирует следующих: очередь продвигается к первому живому" (queue advances to the first LIVE one). A never-validated PR is not live (it can't merge without validation). So the implementation matches the ticket. The comment "the first candidate consumes it" refers to the first *live* candidate. OK.

So if the first validated candidate is not green/not CLEAN, it consumes the slot and does NOT merge, and later validated PRs behind it don't jump it. This matches the BEHIND test ("advance candidate not CLEAN (BEHIND) -> defers, the next PR does not jump it"). Good — FIFO preserved.

Processing: #1 skip → true. #2: armed → reset false. #2 pending fresh → "checks=pending — waiting" continue. #3: deadHeadPassed=false → no advance → FIFO-queued. Correct: live armed head owns the slot; nobody jumps it.

queue: [#1 approved+ai_validating, checks pending 6 min (LIVE armed head),
        #2 blocked, #3 approved+ai_validated, green, CLEAN]
result: merges=[3] — pr-3 merged while pr-1 was actively validating
```

This contradicts the invariant stated 50 lines below: *"An armed PR is a LIVE head by default: it owns the FIFO position and nobody advances past it — unless the stale-pending check below declares it dead."* The regression test (`REGRESSION: live approved head merges first...`) passes only because nothing is interleaved between the armed head and the validated PR.

Consequences are bounded (the merge still passes the full evidence gate, and the jumped armed head goes BEHIND → unarm → refresh → full re-validation), so this is a fairness/churn bug, not an unsafe merge — but it breaks the PR's own FIFO contract in an untested interleaving.

Suggested fix — track whether a live approved-armed head was already seen this tick and stop treating later skips as head-vacating:

```js
var liveArmedSeen = false;
// in the armed branch, after the stale check does NOT fire:
if (approved) liveArmedSeen = true;
// in the blocked branch:
skippedHeads++;
if (!liveArmedSeen) deadHeadPassed = true; // only a skip AHEAD of any live armed head vacates it
```

(A dev-lane/unapproved arm should not set the flag — per `mutexAmong` parity it does not hold the merge window.)

P.S. The same line distorts the new metric: `heads skipped` counts *every* blocked PR in the list, not skipped heads — a healthy tick with one owner-parked PR at the tail logs `heads skipped: 1` (verified). Consider counting only skips that actually vacated a position ahead of waiters.

- **Title**: gh-766 [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-766` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +310
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #766
### Root Cause

A dead PR at mergeBot's FIFO head never yielded its position: a `blocked`-labeled PR was skipped with a bare silent `continue`, and an armed PR with checks pending forever just logged `checks=pending — waiting` on every tick. Every approved PR behind it stayed `FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)` — `acted: 0` for over an hour while 4 approved+validated PRs sat behind `pr-1231` (live, run 37456658085+).

### Fix

- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`:
  - `blocked` head → explicit skip line `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked` (fa #939 semantics preserved — still never acted on); closed PRs were already invisible (open-only listing).
  - Armed **approved** head whose checks have been motionless past `jobParams.staleHeadMinutes` (default 120 = 2h; measured from the oldest pending check run's `started_at`, workflow-run fallback included, missing timestamps fail open) → skip line + unarm `ai_validating`, freeing the SM's validate-armed mutex. Dev-lane arms keep waiting untouched (mutexAmong parity).
  - The first approved PR behind skipped heads that carries the `ai_validated` latch takes the vacated position and merges on the **same evidence gates as the armed path** (green rollup on current head + `CLEAN`). One advance per skip-chain — FIFO holds for everyone behind; never-validated / mid-review / conflicted PRs keep deferring.
  - Metric: `skipped` counter in the result + `heads skipped: N` in the final log line.
- `rollupDetail()` extracted from `checksRollup()` (returns `{ state, pendingSince }`); `checksRollup` behavior unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- `test_mergeBot.js` new suite `dead FIFO head must not starve the queue (gh-766)`: acceptance `[blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → pr-2 merges + head skip line`, stale-pending unarm+advance, fresh-pending no-race, no-timestamp fail-open, live-head regression, BEHIND candidate no-jump, `staleHeadMinutes` knob — RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Full suite: **1663 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

## Understanding the change

### 1. `pendingStartedAt(r)` — new helper
Extracts epoch ms of when a run started (started_at/startedAt/created_at/createdAt). Returns null if unusable. Fails open.

### 2. `rollupDetail()` — extracted from `checksRollup()`
Returns `{ state, pendingSince }`. `checksRollup()` now wraps `rollupDetail().state`. Behavior unchanged.

Note there's a pre-existing weird line in `rollupDetail`:
```js
var runs = cr.check_runs || cr.total_count !== undefined ? (cr.check_runs || []) : [];
```
This is a pre-existing bug (operator precedence) — `cr.check_runs || (cr.total_count !== undefined) ? (cr.check_runs || []) : []`. If `cr.check_runs` is truthy → `(cr.check_runs || [])`. If falsy but `total_count !== undefined` → `[]` (since `cr.check_runs` falsy). If both falsy → `[]`. Actually the result is always `(cr.check_runs || [])` — because both branches of the ternary yield `(cr.check_runs || [])`. So it's a no-op ternary. Pre-existing though — NOT introduced by this PR. The PR didn't change that line. Out-of-diff but could be mentioned in general comments.

### 3. In `action()`:
- New `staleHeadMinutes` param (default 120).
- `skippedHeads` counter, `deadHeadPassed` flag.

Loop changes:
- **blocked label**: now logs `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked`, increments skippedHeads, sets `deadHeadPassed = true`, and continues. Previously bare `continue`.

- **non-validating (or mid-review) branch**: if approved and not agent:review:
  - `advance = deadHeadPassed && labels has ai_validated`
  - if advance: consume `deadHeadPassed`; compute rollup; if green && CLEAN → squashMerge; if merged → acted++, advanced=true; log 🧲
  - if not advanced → the usual FIFO-queued line.

- **armed (validating) branch**: `deadHeadPassed = false;` reset — an armed PR is a live head, nobody advances past it... but wait, there's a subtlety: if `deadHeadPassed` was true and we now encounter an armed PR, `deadHeadPassed` is reset to false. But hold on — should the skip-chain state reset when encountering an armed PR? Consider: blocked head (deadHeadPassed=true), then a mid-review non-approved non-validating PR (the `!validating || agent:review` branch — if NOT approved, no advance attempt; deadHeadPassed stays true), then an armed PR (resets to false). Hmm, if the armed PR comes after, then reset. That seems intentional: the armed PR owns the FIFO position.

  Wait, but there's a subtle bug: `deadHeadPassed = false` reset happens on any armed PR — but what if the armed PR comes first, then blocked? Sequence: armed live head → blocked → then validated candidate. deadHeadPassed gets set true at the blocked PR, which is AFTER the armed one. So the queue advances past the blocked PR to the validated one — correct per gh-766? Hmm, but wait — the ticket's premise: the head of the FIFO queue. The list is sorted by PR number (oldest first = FIFO). The "head" is the first PR. But `deadHeadPassed` doesn't track position; it tracks "some dead PR was skipped earlier in the list". So if there's a healthy armed PR #1 (older), a blocked PR #2, and a validated approved PR #3: tick processes #1 (armed, green, CLEAN, approved) → merges #1. Then #2 blocked → skip line, deadHeadPassed=true. Then #3 validated → advances and merges. So in one tick, TWO merges happen (#1 and #3). Is that intended? The ticket says "One advance per skip-chain". Actually merging both is arguably fine — #1 was ready to merge anyway. But does this violate the mutex semantics (one merge per tick)? Previously, could the bot merge more than one PR per tick? Looking at the loop: for each armed approved green CLEAN PR, it merges. Multiple armed PRs in one tick each merge (the mutex is maintained by SM, not the bot). Actually, the loop iterates all PRs; if several armed approved green CLEAN PRs exist (mutex violation), all merge. So multiple merges per tick are possible pre-existing. OK.

  Now the more significant question: **can a validated PR behind a blocked PR jump ahead of an armed PR that comes later (higher number)?** Sequence: blocked #1 (dead), validated approved #2, armed approved #3 (pending checks). Processing: #1 → skip, deadHeadPassed=true. #2 → advance candidate, merges. deadHeadPassed consumed. #3 → armed, live, waits. Fine.

  But: blocked #1, then NOT-approved un-validated approved PR #2 (no ai_validated), then validated #3. Processing: #1 skip → deadHeadPassed=true. #2: approved, no ai_validated → advance=false → FIFO-queued line; **deadHeadPassed remains true** (not consumed). #3: advance → merges. Hmm — is that correct per "One advance per skip-chain — the first candidate consumes it"? The comment says the first candidate consumes it. But the code only consumes `deadHeadPassed` when `advance` is true (i.e. when deadHeadPassed && ai_validated). If the first approved PR behind the dead head lacks `ai_validated`, it does NOT consume the slot, and the next validated PR takes it. That contradicts the comment "the first candidate consumes it, so FIFO holds for everyone behind; never-validated ... candidates keep deferring". Wait, re-read:

  ```
  // gh-766: dead heads skipped above (blocked / stale-pending)
  // VACATED the head position — the first approved PR behind them
  // that already carries validation evidence (the ai_validated
  // latch) takes the turn on the SAME evidence gates as the armed
  // path: green rollup on the current head + CLEAN. One advance
  // per skip-chain — the first candidate consumes it, so FIFO
  // holds for everyone behind; never-validated, mid-review,
  // draft, conflicted and not-ready candidates keep deferring.
  ```

  So the intent: the first approved PR **that carries ai_validated** takes the turn. PRs without the latch keep deferring and do NOT block a later validated PR from taking the turn? "never-validated ... keep deferring" — meaning they defer but don't consume the slot. Hmm, but that means a validated PR can jump a never-validated approved PR that was queued earlier (FIFO violation in the strict sense). But arguably that's the point: the never-validated PR can't merge anyway (no validation evidence), so letting a fully-evidenced PR merge is the desired outcome. The ticket says "Skipped PR не блокирует следующих: очередь продвигается к первому живому" (queue advances to the first LIVE one). A never-validated PR is not live (it can't merge without validation). So the implementation matches the ticket. The comment "the first candidate consumes it" refers to the first *live* candidate. OK.

  BUT the subtle thing: after a merge-refused or non-green advance candidate — `deadHeadPassed` was consumed (`if (advance) deadHeadPassed = false;`) BEFORE checking green/CLEAN. So if the first validated candidate is not green/not CLEAN, it consumes the slot and does NOT merge, and later validated PRs behind it don't jump it. This matches the BEHIND test ("advance candidate not CLEAN (BEHIND) -> defers, the next PR does not jump it"). Good — FIFO preserved.

  Now — the deadHeadPassed reset in the armed branch: `deadHeadPassed = false;` — placed after the `!validating || agent:review` branch, right before `if (pr.mergeable === false) continue;`. Consider: blocked #1, validated #2 → merges (deadHeadPassed consumed at #2 anyway). Or: blocked #1, armed #2 (pending, fresh), validated #3. Processing: #1 skip → true. #2: armed → reset false. #2 pending fresh → "checks=pending — waiting" continue. #3: deadHeadPassed=false → no advance → FIFO-queued. Correct: live armed head owns the slot; nobody jumps it. 

  Now: what about the stale-pending skip setting deadHeadPassed=true AFTER the reset — order: reset happens first, then rollup computed, then stale check may set deadHeadPassed=true and continue. Then next validated candidate advances. Good.

queue: [#1 approved+ai_validating, checks pending 6 min (LIVE armed head),

This contradicts the invariant stated 50 lines below: *"An armed PR is a LIVE head by default: it owns the FIFO position and nobody advances past it — unless the stale-pending check below declares it dead."* The regression test (`REGRESSION: live approved head merges first...`) passes only because nothing is interleaved between the armed head and the validated PR.

Suggested fix — track whether a live approved-armed head was already seen this tick and stop treating later skips as head-vacating:

```js
var liveArmedSeen = false;
// in the armed branch, after the stale check does NOT fire:
if (approved) liveArmedSeen = true;
// in the blocked branch:
skippedHeads++;
if (!liveArmedSeen) deadHeadPassed = true; // only a skip AHEAD of any live armed head vacates it
```

(A dev-lane/unapproved arm should not set the flag — per `mutexAmong` parity it does not hold the merge window.)

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: oldest-pending staleness un-arms a head whose validation is actively in flight**

`oldestPending` takes the OLDEST `started_at` among pending check runs, but on a single head sha a zombie pending run (runner died, run never re-runs — the documented fa #762 pattern) coexists with the fresh validation run after one unarm → SM re-arm cycle. One stuck run then ages the whole head past `staleHeadMinutes` forever.

Probe (fixture identical to the new suite's `queueFixture`, current branch code):

```
armed approved head, check runs: [IN_PROGRESS started 3h ago (zombie),
                                  IN_PROGRESS started 5 min ago (fresh validation)]
result: removes=[{number:1, label:'ai_validating'}] merges=[2] — queue advanced
        past an IN-FLIGHT validation
```

The `fresh pending armed head (<2h) -> NO advance (in-flight validation is never raced)` guarantee only holds when the fresh run is the *only* pending run. Worse, it is self-perpetuating: the unarm fires → SM re-arms the same sha → the zombie from the previous dispatch is still there → the next tick un-arms again, so the head can never hold its slot long enough to finish a validation while the zombie exists. The workflow-run fallback right above already uses the correct semantics — `mine[0]`, the NEWEST run.

Suggested fix — measure motionlessness from the NEWEST pending evidence (a pending run started within the window means CI is alive):

```js
var st = pendingStartedAt(r);
if (st !== null && (newestPending === null || st > newestPending)) newestPending = st;
```

…and compare `Date.now() - newestPending > staleHeadMinutes * 60 * 1000`. Both existing gh-766 tests still pass under this semantics (single-run cases are unaffected); a mixed zombie+fresh case deserves its own test.

## PR Description

Closes #766
### Root Cause

A dead PR at mergeBot's FIFO head never yielded its position: a `blocked`-labeled PR was skipped with a bare silent `continue`, and an armed PR with checks pending forever just logged `checks=pending — waiting` on every tick. Every approved PR behind it stayed `FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)` — `acted: 0` for over an hour while 4 approved+validated PRs sat behind `pr-1231` (live, run 37456658085+).

### Fix

- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`:
  - `blocked` head → explicit skip line `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked` (fa #939 semantics preserved — still never acted on); closed PRs were already invisible (open-only listing).
  - Armed **approved** head whose checks have been motionless past `jobParams.staleHeadMinutes` (default 120 = 2h; measured from the oldest pending check run's `started_at`, workflow-run fallback included, missing timestamps fail open) → skip line + unarm `ai_validating`, freeing the SM's validate-armed mutex. Dev-lane arms keep waiting untouched (mutexAmong parity).
  - The first approved PR behind skipped heads that carries the `ai_validated` latch takes the vacated position and merges on the **same evidence gates as the armed path** (green rollup on current head + `CLEAN`). One advance per skip-chain — FIFO holds for everyone behind; never-validated / mid-review / conflicted PRs keep deferring.
  - Metric: `skipped` counter in the result + `heads skipped: N` in the final log line.
- `rollupDetail()` extracted from `checksRollup()` (returns `{ state, pendingSince }`); `checksRollup` behavior unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- `test_mergeBot.js` new suite `dead FIFO head must not starve the queue (gh-766)`: acceptance `[blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → pr-2 merges + head skip line`, stale-pending unarm+advance, fresh-pending no-race, no-timestamp fail-open, live-head regression, BEHIND candidate no-jump, `staleHeadMinutes` knob — RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Full suite: **1663 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No SM changes: the bot still only concludes stages whose evidence is already on the PR (merge = approved + validated-latch + green-on-current-head + CLEAN); `mergeStateOf`/`squashMerge` gates are reused verbatim.
- A permanently stuck head now re-validates at most once per threshold period (unarm → SM re-arm) while the queue drains past it each time — bounded CI cost.

# gh-766: [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)

## Description

## Проблема (never-again)

factory-merge.yml (mergeBot) ставит approved PR в FIFO-очередь «awaiting validate-armed turn»; если PR в **голове** очереди никогда не получает validate-armed turn (заблокирован лейблом `blocked` владельцем / checks=pending навсегда / ревьюерский лимб), **вся очередь мёртва за ним**: `acted: 0`, ни один готовый PR не мержится.

Дважды подтверждено в бою на flutter_agent_harness 2026-10-06:
- Утром: pr-1304 approved висел «FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)», очередь стояла, смержился только после ручного вмешательства владельца.
- Днём (run 37456658085 и позже): голова `pr-1231 checks=pending — waiting` (заблокированный владельцем дубль), за ним 4 approved+validated PR (1309, 1311, 1313, 1317) — `acted: 0` на каждом тике больше часа.

## Корень

mergeBot не выкидывает из очереди PR, которые заведомо не получат слот: лейбл `blocked`, checks=pending без движения N часов, closed/superseded. FIFO-голова становится poison pill.

## Предлагаемый фикс

1. На каждом тике голова очереди проверяется на «живость»: `blocked` label / closed / checks=pending старше порога (напр. 2ч) → **skip с явным логом** (не drop молча — строка «⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked» в acted-лог).
2. Skipped PR не блокирует следующих: очередь продвигается к первому живому.
3. Метрика/лог: число пропущенных голов за тик — видно в логе рана (сейчас диагностика требует grep'ать «awaiting validate-armed turn» вручную).

## Acceptance

- Тест/симуляция: очередь [blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → тик мержит approved-2, в логе skip-строка про head.
- Регрессия: нормальный approved-head мержится как раньше.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

This is a pre-existing bug (operator precedence) — `cr.check_runs || (cr.total_count !== undefined) ? (cr.check_runs || []) : []`. If `cr.check_runs` is truthy → `(cr.check_runs || [])`. If falsy but `total_count !== undefined` → `[]` (since `cr.check_runs` falsy). If both falsy → `[]`. Actually the result is always `(cr.check_runs || [])` — because both branches of the ternary yield `(cr.check_runs || [])`. So it's a no-op ternary. Pre-existing though — NOT introduced by this PR. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a blocked PR anywhere in the list vacates the head — even behind a LIVE armed head**

`deadHeadPassed` is set unconditionally for every `blocked` PR in the list, but the flag is consumed by the advance path as "the FIFO *head* position was vacated". When a blocked PR sits **behind** a live armed head, a validated PR behind the blocked one jumps the live head and merges in the same tick.

Probe (fixture identical to the new suite's `queueFixture`, current branch code):

```
queue: [#1 approved+ai_validating, checks pending 6 min (LIVE armed head),
        #2 blocked, #3 approved+ai_validated, green, CLEAN]
result: merges=[3] — pr-3 merged while pr-1 was actively validating
```

This contradicts the invariant stated 50 lines below: *"An armed PR is a LIVE head by default: it owns the FIFO position and nobody advances past it — unless the stale-pending check below declares it dead."* The regression test (`REGRESSION: live approved head merges first...`) passes only because nothing is interleaved between the armed head and the validated PR.

Consequences are bounded (the merge still passes the full evidence gate, and the jumped armed head goes BEHIND → unarm → refresh → full re-validation), so this is a fairness/churn bug, not an unsafe merge — but it breaks the PR's own FIFO contract in an untested interleaving.

Suggested fix — track whether a live approved-armed head was already seen this tick and stop treating later skips as head-vacating:

```js
var liveArmedSeen = false;
// in the armed branch, after the stale check does NOT fire:
if (approved) liveArmedSeen = true;
// in the blocked branch:
skippedHeads++;
if (!liveArmedSeen) deadHeadPassed = true; // only a skip AHEAD of any live armed head vacates it
```

(A dev-lane/unapproved arm should not set the flag — per `mutexAmong` parity it does not hold the merge window.)

P.S. The same line distorts the new metric: `heads skipped` counts *every* blocked PR in the list, not skipped heads — a healthy tick with one owner-parked PR at the tail logs `heads skipped: 1` (verified). Consider counting only skips that actually vacated a position ahead of waiters.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 768
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/768
- **Title**: gh-766 [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-766` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +310
- **Deletions**: -31
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T13:45:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #766
### Root Cause

A dead PR at mergeBot's FIFO head never yielded its position: a `blocked`-labeled PR was skipped with a bare silent `continue`, and an armed PR with checks pending forever just logged `checks=pending — waiting` on every tick. Every approved PR behind it stayed `FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)` — `acted: 0` for over an hour while 4 approved+validated PRs sat behind `pr-1231` (live, run 37456658085+).

### Fix

- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`:
  - `blocked` head → explicit skip line `⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked` (fa #939 semantics preserved — still never acted on); closed PRs were already invisible (open-only listing).
  - Armed **approved** head whose checks have been motionless past `jobParams.staleHeadMinutes` (default 120 = 2h; measured from the oldest pending check run's `started_at`, workflow-run fallback included, missing timestamps fail open) → skip line + unarm `ai_validating`, freeing the SM's validate-armed mutex. Dev-lane arms keep waiting untouched (mutexAmong parity).
  - The first approved PR behind skipped heads that carries the `ai_validated` latch takes the vacated position and merges on the **same evidence gates as the armed path** (green rollup on current head + `CLEAN`). One advance per skip-chain — FIFO holds for everyone behind; never-validated / mid-review / conflicted PRs keep deferring.
  - Metric: `skipped` counter in the result + `heads skipped: N` in the final log line.
- `rollupDetail()` extracted from `checksRollup()` (returns `{ state, pendingSince }`); `checksRollup` behavior unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- `test_mergeBot.js` new suite `dead FIFO head must not starve the queue (gh-766)`: acceptance `[blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → pr-2 merges + head skip line`, stale-pending unarm+advance, fresh-pending no-race, no-timestamp fail-open, live-head regression, BEHIND candidate no-jump, `staleHeadMinutes` knob — RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Full suite: **1663 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No SM changes: the bot still only concludes stages whose evidence is already on the PR (merge = approved + validated-latch + green-on-current-head + CLEAN); `mergeStateOf`/`squashMerge` gates are reused verbatim.
- A permanently stuck head now re-validates at most once per threshold period (unarm → SM re-arm) while the queue drains past it each time — bounded CI cost.

# gh-766: [BUG] mergeBot FIFO: заблокированный/stale PR в голове очереди парализует весь merge pipeline (acted: 0)

## Description

## Проблема (never-again)

factory-merge.yml (mergeBot) ставит approved PR в FIFO-очередь «awaiting validate-armed turn»; если PR в **голове** очереди никогда не получает validate-armed turn (заблокирован лейблом `blocked` владельцем / checks=pending навсегда / ревьюерский лимб), **вся очередь мёртва за ним**: `acted: 0`, ни один готовый PR не мержится.

Дважды подтверждено в бою на flutter_agent_harness 2026-10-06:
- Утром: pr-1304 approved висел «FIFO-queued (awaiting validate-armed turn)», очередь стояла, смержился только после ручного вмешательства владельца.
- Днём (run 37456658085 и позже): голова `pr-1231 checks=pending — waiting` (заблокированный владельцем дубль), за ним 4 approved+validated PR (1309, 1311, 1313, 1317) — `acted: 0` на каждом тике больше часа.

## Корень

mergeBot не выкидывает из очереди PR, которые заведомо не получат слот: лейбл `blocked`, checks=pending без движения N часов, closed/superseded. FIFO-голова становится poison pill.

## Предлагаемый фикс

1. На каждом тике голова очереди проверяется на «живость»: `blocked` label / closed / checks=pending старше порога (напр. 2ч) → **skip с явным логом** (не drop молча — строка «⏭️ pr-N skipped: blocked» в acted-лог).
2. Skipped PR не блокирует следующих: очередь продвигается к первому живому.
3. Метрика/лог: число пропущенных голов за тик — видно в логе рана (сейчас диагностика требует grep'ать «awaiting validate-armed turn» вручную).

## Acceptance

- Тест/симуляция: очередь [blocked-head, approved-2, approved-3] → тик мержит approved-2, в логе skip-строка про head.
- Регрессия: нормальный approved-head мержится как раньше.

## Machine jobs
